name: Question 8
problem: Find all of the subsets of $T={1,2,3}.$
worked_solution:
To find every subset of $T,$ we list out every combination of elements within $T.$ 

We can use the following diagram to visualize the process:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14038640/assets/127ee1187ebf3a2cc498c88326285d5adf5d609cf3276885e8c9d525435133eb.png)

Note that we must include the empty set since it is a subset of every set.

By doing this, we get

$$
∅,\,{1},\,{2},\,{3},\,{1,2},\,{1,3},\,{2,3},\,{1,2,3}.
$$

html:
Question 8
?

Find all of the subsets of T={1,2,3}.

a
∅,{1},{2},{3},{1,2},{1,3},{2,3},{1,2,3}
b
∅,{1},{2},{3}
c
{1},{2},{3},{1,2},{1,3},{2,3},{1,2,3}
d
∅,{1},{2},{3},{1,2},{1,3},{2,3}
e
∅,{1},{2},{3}{1,2,3}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find every subset of T, we list out every combination of elements within T.

We can use the following diagram to visualize the process:

Note that we must include the empty set since it is a subset of every set.

By doing this, we get

∅,{1},{2},{3},{1,2},{1,3},{2,3},{1,2,3}.
